title: SAML assertion merging causes transient over-grant and missing audit entries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer report: intermittent permission grants observed after SAML-based account linking for some enterprise customers. In several cases a user briefly received elevated project-level permissions that were not reflected in the audit trail. The issue appears when two SAML assertions (group attributes) are merged during session/link reconciliation and our merge order causes a transient over-grant while audit logging records only the final state. This ticket tracks investigation, fix, and remediation steps.
reproduction_steps: 1) Customer config: SAML IdP emits group claims across two separate assertions during login (partial attributes in initial assertion, remaining groups in later assertion as part of linking flow)
2) Create an account that triggers the linking flow (SAML relay + SCIM patch) where groups A and B arrive in separate assertions
3) Observe that RBAC v2 applies a temporary rule resolution where an intermediate merge applies a permissive evaluation (project:admin) before final reconciliation
4) Check /api/admin/audit (or external audit sink) and note missing entry for the intermediate grant — audit shows only the later deny or final assignment
5) Reproduce flakily in staging by simulating out-of-order assertion delivery and network latency between auth-proxy and identity-service
technical_summary: Root cause: the identity service performs a non-atomic two-step attribute merge when handling incremental SAML assertions during account linking. We currently apply changes to the RBAC store in-place between steps and emit audit events only after the final write. Because permission evaluation runs against the intermediate state, requests can observe a permissive transient state. Two contributing issues: 1) merge is order-dependent and not idempotent; 2) audit emission is tied to final write rather than every state transition. Fix approach: convert merge to deterministic set-union semantics (no transient permissive state), make the update atomic (apply-before-evaluate guard), and emit structured audit events for every assertion processed (include assertion IDs and timestamps). Also add schema versioning to audit records to make post-hoc analysis reliable.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic merge implementation merged to main with unit tests covering out-of-order assertions
No transient permission elevation observable in staging under assertion reordering tests (1000 simulated runs)
Audit entries created for every processed assertion with original assertion_id and raw attributes
Canary rollout shows zero new customer escalations for customers previously affected
Post-deploy audit comparison job demonstrates repairability for historical gaps
mitigation_steps: Short-term: enable an emergency policy to reject incremental SAML assertions for affected customers (feature-flagged) and recommend IdP to include all groups in a single assertion
Immediate: run a targeted ACL revoke job for customers where we confirmed over-grant, invalidate active session tokens tied to the affected workspace
Monitoring: add synthetic checks that exercise linking flow and assert no temporary admin access is granted
Communication: notify impacted customers with recommended mitigation steps and ETA for fix
rollout_plan: 1) Change implementation in identity service: atomic-merge + deterministic union + emit per-assertion audit events
2) Merge PR and run CI; add new unit/integration tests that fuzz assertion ordering
3) Deploy to canary nodes (10% traffic) for 24h and run synthetic test harness
4) If green, promote to 50% then 100% with monitoring runbook and on-call engineer assigned
5) Run audit-consistency job to surface historical inconsistencies and schedule repair/communication
qa_plan: Add deterministic test fixture with interleaved assertions A and B and assert no temporary admin grant
Fuzz test: randomize assertion delivery timing for 10k iterations in CI
Integration test: full e2e with auth-proxy, identity-service, and rbac-evaluator in docker-compose
Manual verification: repro script used by Support to confirm fix on customer staging instance
